(a) **Differential Rate Expression Method:** 
The rate of a reaction is given by $r = -\frac{d[A]}{dt} = k[A]^n$. Taking logarithms on both sides: $\log\left(-\frac{d[A]}{dt}\right) = \log k + n \log[A]$. By plotting $\log(-\frac{d[A]}{dt})$ versus $\log[A]$, a straight line is obtained where the slope gives the order of the reaction ($n$) and the intercept gives $\log k$.

(b) **Numerical Calculation for Second Order Reaction:**
Initial concentration, $a = 0.2 \text{ mol/L}$.
Reaction is $30\%$ complete, so amount reacted $x = 0.30 \times 0.2 = 0.06 \text{ mol/L}$.
Concentration remaining at time $t = 50 \text{ min}$, $(a - x) = 0.2 - 0.06 = 0.14 \text{ mol/L}$.

The second-order rate constant formula is:
$$k = \frac{1}{t} \left(\frac{x}{a(a-x)}\right)$$
$$k = \frac{1}{50 \text{ min}} \left(\frac{0.06}{0.2 \times 0.14}\right) = \frac{1}{50} \left(\frac{0.06}{0.028}\right) = \frac{2.1428}{50} = 0.0428 \text{ L mol}^{-1} \text{ min}^{-1}$$
proTip: Always include proper units for the rate constant based on the overall reaction order.
